subject: [PATCH v5 0/8] mm/gup: walk and batch whole PTE tables in slow GUP

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary: Reviewer requested a normal diffstat like every other series to easily identify changes and their impact on the codebase.
reviews.raw_body:
I'm glad you describe it here, but could we please just have a normal diffstat
like every other series? I feel like I've asked you this before :)

I really hate a missing diffstat in the _usual_ form because it makes it hard to
glance at it and know what's touched (and pretty much 100% of the time it turns
out the diffstat is v. large when this happens...)

Here it is for this one:

 mm/gup.c | 573 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 1 file changed, 347 insertions(+), 226 deletions(-)

--
Cheers, Lorenzo

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary:
Lorenzo noted that the patch does not handle the case where there is no PMD entry, and suggested adding a comment to clarify this special handling.

Reviewer Lorenzo expressed concerns about unclear and redundant comments in the patch, specifically pointing out a permanent comment referencing 'the old code' without clear context, as well as a check for pte_none() followed by an additional write check, which he considers unnecessary. He also questioned the handling of page cache access in no_page_table(), suggesting it may be specific to hugetlbfs and potentially breaking other callers.

Reviewer Lorenzo pointed out that the fpb_flags parameter, which is used to select the scan type in the batch-length helper, is set true but not used anywhere, and suggested removing it as dead code.

Reviewer Lorenzo expressed confusion about the patch's handling of need_no_page_table and suggested an alternative implementation, also questioning whether the changes constitute a genuine cleanup.
reviews.raw_body:
OK so this is what happens if there's no PMD entry. Maybe worth a comment?
Especially if you have special handling for the PTE PTL being held below.

---

This feels -- a little -- schloppy ;)

Why are you referencing 'the old code' in a permanent comment for which what
'the old code' means is super unclear?

That's really just not helpful.

'A none PTE returns from gup_lookup_pte() before any write check runs' also
reads weirdly.

I'm also not sure why you're sending a pte_none() PTE to gup_lookup_pte()
anyway + checking for the error again?

	if (pte_none(ptep)) {
		... whatever ...
		goto blah;
	}

It seems silly otherwise.


Also isn't the page cache thing _only_ for hugetlbfs, unless you changed
that? And aren't a number of other callers of no_page_table() also broken?

But in general the comment could be made much clearer:

	/*
	 * If a hugetlb VMA it might access the page cache in no_page_table(),
	 * which cannot be done under the PTL, so defer until it's dropped.
	 */

Or whatever, something human-written like that :)

---

This is set true but not used anywhere? This is dead code no? Am I missing
something?

Patches should be incremental but adding completely useless locals incrementally
seems silly?

---

I'm guessing you forgot to include the code that works with
need_no_page_table here?

Should it have been:

	if (!ret && need_no_page_table)
		return no_page_table(vma, flags, address);

Perhaps?

I'm not sure any of this is really a cleanup, I'm finding this quite
confusing, actually...

'need_no_page_table' isn't a great name either. Maybe is_none or something?

2026-11-17.patch_summary: This patch series improves the performance of slow GUP (get user pages) by batching whole PTE tables and reducing the number of refcount grabs. The current implementation resolves and commits one PTE per call, leading to a restart of the page table descent and re-taking of the PTE lock for every page. This patch series brings the slow path in line with the fast path, which already batches PTE-mapped large folios. The patches include refactors, helper functions, and changes to follow_page_pte() and gup_lookup_pte(). The result is a significant performance improvement, with median get times reduced by up to 12.8x for mTHP (large memory pages) and 2.3x for base pages.
